'''Ruth S. DeFries''' (born October 20, 1956) is an American [[Environmental geography|environmental geographer]] who specializes in the use of [[remote sensing]] to study Earth's habitability under the influence of human activities, such as [[deforestation]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-7451676_ITM|title=Maryland-Led Research Revises Estimates of Tropical Deforestation.|date=2002-10-14|publisher=Ascribe Higher Education News Service|accessdate=2008-09-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2001/06/010605072649.htm|title=An Improved Method For Monitoring National And Global Deforestation|date=2001-06-05|publisher=ScienceDaily|accessdate=2008-09-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2006/09/060920092900.htm|title=Growth In Amazon Cropland May Impact Climate And Deforestation Patterns|date=2006-09-22|publisher=ScienceDaily|accessdate=2008-09-16}}</ref> that influence regulating [[Biophysics|biophysical]] and [[Biogeochemistry|biogeochemical]] processes.<ref name="BIO">{{cite web|url=http://www.earth.columbia.edu/ac/bios/defries.html|title=Ruth DeFries biography|publisher=The Earth Institute, Columbia University|accessdate=2008-09-16}}</ref> She was one of 24 recipients of the 2007 [[MacArthur Fellowship]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.2913825/apps/nl/content2.asp?content_id={FACCE0E3-8520-4752-9B5D-0F05779C3340}&notoc=1|title=MacArthur Fellows 2007|publisher=The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation|accessdate=2008-09-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-32968352_ITM|title='Genius' rewarded: Hopkins physician, UM geographer are among 24 awarded $500,000 MacArthur grants for research.|date=2007-09-25|publisher=Baltimore Sun|accessdate=2008-09-16 | first1=Frank D. | last1=Roylance | first2=Chris | last2=Emery}}</ref> and was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newsdesk.umd.edu/scitech/release.cfm?ArticleID=1277|title=A Conversation with UM's Ruth DeFries, Newly Elected to the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=University of Maryland|accessdate=2008-09-16|archive-date=2008-12-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219083739/http://www.newsdesk.umd.edu/scitech/release.cfm?ArticleID=1277|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Life==
DeFries received her Ph.D. in 1980 from the Department of Geography and [[Environmental Engineering]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]] and her B.A. in Earth Science in 1976 from [[Washington University in St. Louis]]. In April 2016, [[Columbia University]] named her a University Professor, its highest academic rank. She had previously been the Denning Family Professor of [[Sustainable Development]] in [[Columbia University|Columbia]]'s Department of [[Ecology]], [[Evolution]], and [[Environmental Biology]]. Before moving to Columbia in 2008, she was a professor at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] with joint appointments in the Department of Geography and the Earth System Science Interdisciplinary Center.<ref name="BIO"/>

==An Ecomodernist Manifesto==
In April 2015, DeFries joined with a group of scholars in issuing ''An [[Ecomodernist Manifesto]]''.<ref name=EcoModernistManifesto>{{cite web|title=An Ecomodernist Manifesto|url=http://www.ecomodernism.org/manifesto/|website=ecomodernism.org|accessdate=April 17, 2015|quote=A good Anthropocene demands that humans use their growing social, economic, and technological powers to make life better for people, stabilize the climate, and protect the natural world.}}</ref><ref name=NYT41415>{{cite news|author1=Eduardo Porter|title=A Call to Look Past Sustainable Development|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/04/15/business/an-environmentalist-call-to-look-past-sustainable-development.html|accessdate=April 17, 2015|work=The New York Times|date=April 14, 2015|quote=On Tuesday, a group of scholars involved in the environmental debate, including Professor Roy and Professor Brook, Ruth DeFries of Columbia University, and Michael Shellenberger and Ted Nordhaus of the Breakthrough Institute in Oakland, Calif., issued what they are calling the "Eco-modernist Manifesto."}}</ref> The other authors were: John Asafu-Adjaye, Linus Blomqvist, [[Stewart Brand]], [[Barry Brook (scientist)|Barry Brook]], [[Erle Ellis]], Christopher Foreman, [[David Keith (scientist)|David Keith]], Martin Lewis, [[Mark Lynas]], [[Ted Nordhaus]], [[Roger A. Pielke, Jr.]], Rachel Pritzker, Joyashree Roy, Mark Sagoff, [[Michael Shellenberger]], [[Robert Stone (director)|Robert Stone]], and Peter Teague<ref name=EcoModernismAuthors>{{cite web|title=Authors An Ecomodernist Manifesto|url=http://www.ecomodernism.org/authors/|website=ecomodernism.org|accessdate=April 17, 2015|quote=As scholars, scientists, campaigners, and citizens, we write with the conviction that knowledge and technology, applied with wisdom, might allow for a good, or even great, [[Anthropocene]].}}</ref>

== Works ==

=== Books ===
* The Big Ratchet: How Humanity Thrives in the Face of Natural Crisis (2014) Basic Books<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ruthdefries.com/book/big-ratchet/|title=The Big Ratchet|last=DeFries|first=Ruth|website=Ruth DeFries}}</ref>

=== Scientific papers ===
DeFries is the author or co-author of over 100 scientific papers on such topics as: impacts of tropical fires on air quality and [[greenhouse gas emissions]]; land use, nutrition, and food security; land use and conservation in the tropics; climate and tropical agriculture; processes of tropical deforestation and degradation; methods for remote sensing of land cover; and reviews and conceptual papers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ruthdefries.e3b.columbia.edu/publications/|title=Publications|last=DeFries|first=Ruth|website=Columbia University}}</ref>
